name: Layered-Photo Parallax Hero
summary: The hero scene is assembled from photographic depth planes — background plate, midground subject, foreground cutout props — that drift at different rates on scroll and cursor move, producing a diorama sense of 3D depth from 2D imagery. This is the industry's core imagery-first method (PLAN §1): pre-rendered plates choreographed with parallax, not realtime geometry.

composition: 3-5 explicit planes, no more: far scenery, midground subject, foreground props; each plane owns a distinct silhouette so separation reads instantly.
Foreground elements can frame the composition like a natural vignette or portal (cliffs, arches, props at frame edges).
The subject holds a stable anchor while satellite planes carry the motion; typography usually lives between mid and foreground so objects can interlock with it.
layering: Depth comes from clean background-free cutouts stacked with scale/offset — a can plus a separate shadow plate plus floating props reads as more dimensional than one flat photo.
Parallax rate encodes depth: background slowest, foreground fastest; a plane moving at the wrong rate for its apparent distance instantly breaks the illusion.
Slight per-plane blur or atmospheric haze on far planes sells distance better than scale alone.
Shadows are their own plates — detached, softened, and moved independently of the object casting them.
lighting: Light is baked into the photography — golden meadow, beach glow, overcast snow; the composite must match light TEMPERATURE and direction across planes or the collage falls apart.
A gentle scrim or vignette behind copy zones protects legibility without flattening the scene.
Glow/haze planes between cutouts act as atmosphere and hide seam artifacts.
typography: Type is treated as one of the depth planes (see oversized-type-editorial) — occluded by foreground, occluding background.
Copy stays minimal; the scene is the message.

rules: The palette comes FROM the plates — natural photographic color, optionally re-graded per scene/theme; UI chrome stays neutral so any plate set drops in.
When scenes swap (seasons, flavors, destinations) the grade itself carries the mood shift while layout stays constant.

easing: Soft damped glides — planes ease to rest with expo-out settles; no bounce, the planes have photographic mass.
Cursor-driven parallax uses viscous follow (lag), never 1:1 tracking.
pacing: Scroll-driven and moderately paced; each composed state holds long enough to read before the next resolves.
Idle states keep a barely-perceptible drift so the diorama never freezes into a flat image.
choreography: Layers stagger by depth: background shifts first/slowest, foreground props fastest — the stagger IS the depth cue.
Scene changes restage all planes together (crossfade or fly-in cascade) while the layout skeleton stays fixed.

gapNotes: PrismNode already carries renderMode 'parallax-plane' + depthMapUrl, and FLUX generates the source imagery — but the R2 composite pipeline (automated background removal/cutout, depth-map extraction, per-plane relight and unified color grade) is W-PHOTO scope.
Detached shadow plates and seam-hiding haze layers have no authoring primitive yet; today they must be hand-assembled.
Cross-plane light-direction matching is unverified — no gate checks that composited planes share light temperature.

whenToUse: Product heroes where photoreal quality matters more than free-angle interaction — this route maximizes realism per byte (PLAN §1).
Narrative scenes (seasons, places, moods) that swap plate sets over a constant layout.
Any brief that supplies or generates strong photography.
whenNotToUse: Objects needing free rotation/inspection — that is R1/R4 territory; parallax planes break past ~15° of implied camera movement.
Content-dense utility pages; heavy hero plates tax load time.
When source imagery is weak — the family amplifies photographic quality, good or bad.

notes: The most load-bearing family in the corpus: 5 of 17 deep sources build on it, and the zero-point teardown in the PLAN identified it as the industry's actual photoreal method.
Avoid stacking a second full-screen shader effect over the plates — the composite already spends the motion budget; fluid/glitch overlays fight the depth read.

antiRepetition.notes: Same cluster as levitating-product-hero and cutout-product-cascade-hero — all are cutout-plate composites; offer one per option set.

sources.title: Zero Point Energy Drink Showcase (PLAN §1 teardown)
sources.motionEvidence: Founder live analysis recorded in PRISM-DESIGN-SUPREMACY-PLAN.md §1: identified as layered photographic/pre-rendered cutouts (can + separate shadow plate + floating fruit PNGs + four full-bleed background plates) choreographed with motion/parallax + post — NOT realtime 3D. Corroborated by the monitor session's live-demo observation of the ambient orbit loop.
